set.body:
Real-data screenshot review at bbb9d49a found that the separate ScanpathWorkbench is functional but does not yet use the shared Studio design system. At 1440x900 the result and failure tables are readable, but the convention paragraph is dense and the native controls/table typography differ from the main Studio UI.

Code evidence: studio/desktop/src/main/scala/eyes4s/studio/desktop/scanpath/ScanpathWorkbench.scala constructs literal button, table, status and convention strings, uses local padding, and disables controls without DisabledReason.attach. Its scene setup must be checked for shared theme/type/control installation. This is a design-parity follow-up, not a numerical failure.

Acceptance: establish the spec/board source for this separate workspace before claiming board parity; route all visible strings through text ids; use Tokens, TypeCss and shared control/table styles; attach visible disabled reasons; apply CompositeFocus and keyboard-only focus rings to both tables. Preserve explicit convention and unavailable-pair information in a less dense hierarchy. Verify synthetic fixtures in both themes at ordinary and narrow widths, keyboard traversal/home-row focus, disabled reasons, all five component results and save/reopen. Keep private study data and screenshots out of committed fixtures. Update PARITY_CHECKLIST with the agreed scope. Split broader integration into the main application into its own slice if needed.

The private numerical validation remains on its frozen source tree; no UI source changes are included in that evidence.
set.title: Studio: bring the separate MultiMatch workspace under the shared design system
